reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that a liquid precursor method can produce ultrafine high-entropy diboride powders at 1800 °C, but it does not address pure ZrB2, densification behavior, or resistance to liquid plating baths. The key premises about molecular mixing, lower-temperature densification, and improved service performance for ZrB2 are therefore unsupported by the provided passage.
premises: Liquid precursor method enables molecular-level mixing of Zr and B sources
Molecular mixing reduces diffusion distances and promotes densification at lower temperature (~1800 °C)
Lower-temperature densification yields ultrafine grains and reduced porosity in ZrB2
Denser, ultrafine microstructure resists liquid infiltration and corrosive attack in a plating bath
The cited evidence (E1) supports the effectiveness of liquid precursor methods for reducing sintering temperature in similar boride systems
